method: Items are published only when an official primary source or at least two independent publishers support them.

items.headline: Prime Minister Hung holds talks in Vientiane on first Laos and Cambodia trip
items.summary: Prime Minister Le Minh Hung began an official visit to Laos on 8 October, the first leg of a trip to Laos and Cambodia running 8 to 10 October, according to Viet Nam's foreign ministry. Viet Nam News reported that 11 cooperation documents were signed. Cambodia's foreign ministry confirmed the Cambodia leg for 9 and 10 October.
items.note: The figure of 11 documents comes from Viet Nam News only. Outcomes of the Cambodia leg were not yet reported at the time of writing.

sources.evidence: The two sides signed 11 cooperation documents on this occasion.

items.headline: Party Central Committee closes fourth plenum with talent strategy and 2027 targets
items.summary: The 14th Party Central Committee closed its fourth plenum in Hanoi on 8 October after four days, according to Viet Nam News. It adopted a personnel resolution and a national strategy on attracting talent in key sectors, and discussed 2027 targets of GDP growth of at least 10 percent and average inflation of about 4.5 percent.
items.note: Closing outcomes and 2027 target figures are from Viet Nam News (state-run). The other sources confirm the agenda, including the talent strategy and 2027 plan, not the final figures.

items.headline: Viet Nam and Panama issue joint statement after presidential visit
items.summary: Panama's President Jose Raul Mulino made an official visit to Viet Nam from 5 to 8 October, and the two sides issued a joint statement on 7 October. VietnamPlus reported that ten cooperation documents were exchanged or signed, covering maritime transport, customs, agriculture and tourism, and that talks on an investment promotion and protection agreement will follow.
items.note: Panama America reports nine agreements and memoranda signed by the foreign ministers, while VietnamPlus reports ten documents. The count differs by source.

items.headline: Viet Nam records third-quarter GDP growth of 9.95 percent
items.summary: According to the National Statistics Office, GDP grew 9.95 percent year on year in the third quarter of 2026 and 9.01 percent in the first nine months. The Nation (Thailand) reported that the Q3 figure exceeded the 8.65 percent median in a Bloomberg survey of economists, and that the government targets full-year growth of at least 10 percent.
items.note: Figures are preliminary estimates of the statistics office.

items.headline: Goods trade turns to surplus in September, nine-month deficit at 19.42 billion dollars
items.summary: The National Statistics Office reported a goods trade surplus of 1.27 billion US dollars in September after nine consecutive monthly deficits. For January to September, exports were 434.30 billion dollars and imports 453.72 billion, leaving a deficit of 19.42 billion dollars on total turnover of 888.02 billion, up 30.4 percent.
items.note: Preliminary figures of the statistics office. The September surplus figure is from VietnamPlus citing the office.

items.headline: Viet Nam consumer prices rise 5.08 percent year on year in September
items.summary: According to the National Statistics Office, consumer prices in September 2026 were 5.08 percent higher than a year earlier and 0.62 percent higher than in August. The average index for the first nine months was 4.52 percent above the same period of 2025. The government's stated inflation target for the year is 4.5 percent, per Viet Nam News.
items.note: Index values of 105.08, 100.62 and 104.52 were converted to percentage changes. The 4.5 percent target is cited by Viet Nam News on 28 September, outside the reporting window.

items.headline: Registered foreign direct investment rises 76.4 percent in first nine months
items.summary: According to the National Statistics Office, total registered inward foreign direct investment reached 50.36 billion US dollars from 1 January to 30 September 2026, up 76.4 percent year on year. Disbursed foreign investment was 21.07 billion dollars, up 12.1 percent.
items.note: Preliminary figures of one agency. Registered capital covers pledges and may differ from realised investment.
